21 22 > **Automation proposes. Editorial state decides. Published artifacts must match the current state.** 23 24 ## What it does well 25 26 ### It erases text without wrecking the art 27 28 Cleanup runs on a mask of the letters themselves, not on detector rectangles. A comic-text-detector mask head reads the letters; the app adds a thin outline round every letter, then grows into the glow and shadow round it. Art that touches the letters stays. 29 30 Two whole webtoon chapters on a 4-core GitHub runner, real models, 2 page workers (evidence on the `audit-evidence` branch): 31 32 | Chapter | Slices | Text blocks | Time | Text left | 33 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 34 | The World After the End, ch. 254 | 68 | 167 | 418 s | **0** | 35 | Youngest Scion of the Mages, ch. 137 | 52 | 145 | 332 s | **0** | 36 37 Times move with the runner's CPU: the first chapter took 418 s and 446 s on two different CPU models. 38 39 On labelled synthetic text, the mask erases 73.7 % of what has to go at 73.1 % precision; the hand-tuned rules it replaced managed 65.4 % at 43.1 %. 40 41 ### The same image always gives the same result 42 43 A page cleaned twice gives the same pixels, on any CPU: the sampled slices of a whole chapter came out pixel-identical on two different CPU models. The one source of run-to-run drift, a random seed in the background-colour clustering, is fixed. 44 45 ### It is fast where it matters 46 47 - A 2.4 M-parameter detector finds the text of a slice in a few packed passes (halves side by side, near-native bands, page-scale columns for big captions), on the OpenVINO runtime when available. 48 - The letter-mask model runs about 40× faster than the released one with identical masks. 49 - LaMa fills each region in one downscaled pass (512 px long side), and only where a fill is needed: a hole ringed by one colour, of any shade, is filled flat with no model run. 50 51 ### The whole chapter runs on a laptop 52 53 Everything on the cleanup path is a small ONNX model on the CPU. Nothing needs a GPU or a cloud account; OCR and AI translation are optional layers around that. 54 55 ## Two ways to work 56 57 **By hand.** Import a chapter and clean it, then correct, OCR, translate and letter it in the browser workbench. Every step can be redone. 58 59 **A.I mode.** Paste a chapter URL with an AI key (or use Manga Cloud) and pick the target language: Vietnamese, English, Indonesian, Spanish, Portuguese, French or German. Source-page identity and stitch ownership are recorded, so the chapter is rebuilt with no duplicated or missing pixels. 94 95 ### Detection 96 97 The Kiuyha ONNX text detector (`models/kiuyha_text_1280.onnx`) finds the text blocks of a slice. See [docs/comic-fonts.md](docs/comic-fonts.md). 141 142 ### AI providers 143 144 Built in: Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenAI and OpenRouter. 1	# PPTX generation with python-pptx — deck-lab field notes
     2	
     3	name: pptx
     4	description: Build clean 16:9 PowerPoint decks with python-pptx from scratch (no template): layout grid, palette, fonts/sizes, transitions, charts, and a render-then-measure QA loop that catches text overflow, overlapping boxes, tiny fonts and low-contrast colors. Use when creating or fixing a .pptx deck.
     5	
     6	## Workflow (the loop that actually worked)
     7	
     8	1. Write the generator script in one pass with a **fixed canvas** and **helper functions** (below). Do not hand-place every shape with raw `Inches()` — centralize the grid.
     9	2. Save the `.pptx`, then render and *measure*, don't just eyeball:
    10	   ```bash
    11	   soffice -env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/lo_profile --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir out deck.pptx
    12	   pdftoppm -png -r 50 out/deck.pdf out/slide      # 50 dpi is enough to spot overflow
    13	   ```
    14	   The `-env:UserInstallation` flag is required in this sandbox (otherwise LibreOffice's profile write fails).
    15	3. Run `check_deck.py` on the pptx: it flags text that likely overflows its box, textboxes overlapping other text, fonts under 12pt, and contrast ratios under 3.0 (WCAG large-text minimum).
    16	4. Open 2-3 rendered slides with view_image to confirm the checker's flags match what the eye sees (the checker is a heuristic — char-width estimate — so a false positive is possible; a true visual clip is not).
    17	5. Fix in the generator, not the pptx; rerun 2-4 until `check_deck.py` prints "clean".
    18	
    19	## Layout: 16:9 grid
    20	
    21	- Slide is **13.333 × 7.5 in** (set `prs.slide_width`/`slide_height` — never trust the template).
    22	- One **margin** of 0.6in on all sides → content width 12.13in. All x-coordinates come from `MARGIN` + column offsets; all y from a running cursor or named zones.
    23	- Named zones (16:9, top→bottom): title band 0.4–1.5in (kicker + title + accent rule), content 1.8–6.8in, footer/page 6.9–7.3in. Never start content above 1.8in — the header zone owns 0.4–1.6in.
    24	- For card grids: 3 cards = 3.8in wide × 4.17in pitch (0.37in gutter); 4 stats = 2.85in wide × 3.13in pitch. Row height ≤ 1.0in for list items, ≤ 2.4in for cards with a title + 3 lines of body.
    25	- A slide with more than ~5 text blocks is too dense: split it. Six to eight slides total is the target for a short deck; each slide gets ONE idea.
    26	
    27	## Colors
    28	
    29	- Light theme: bg `#F7F9FC`, ink `#1F2430`, accent `#0F62FE`, muted `#5B6474`, panel `#E8EEF9`. Dark theme: invert — bg `#0F1420`, ink `#E8EDF5`, accent `#4D9FFF`, panel `#1B2436`.
    30	- **Contrast is a hard rule, not taste**: body text ≥ 4.5:1, large text (≥18pt) ≥ 3:1 against the background it actually sits on. The checker computes this — let it. Common failure: white text on a panel that is "almost white" (contrast 1.0–1.5, invisible). If text sits on a filled panel, contrast is text-vs-panel, not text-vs-slide.
    31	- Muted/secondary text: never go lighter than `#5B6474` on light bg (`#7a7a7a` is the practical floor; `#9aa` fails for body size).
    32	- One accent per deck, max two colors of accent (accent + a success/warn if needed). Do not introduce a third hue per slide.
    33	
    34	## Fonts & sizes (what fits on 13.33in at 16:9)
    35	
    36	| Role | Size | Notes |
    37	|---|---|---|
    38	| Kicker/eyebrow | 13–14, bold, accent color, ALL CAPS | one line max |
    39	| Slide title | 30–34 | one line max; keep under 34 or it wraps |
    40	| Card/section heading | 18–20 | |
    41	| Body | 15–16 | 15pt is the smallest comfortable body size at 50% zoom |
    42	| Big stat number | 28–32 | |
    43	| Caption under stat | 12–13 | |
    44	
    45	- Hard floor 12pt for anything; floor 14pt for body. If you need more than one caption line, widen the box before shrinking the font.
    46	- A line of 16pt Segoe UI holds roughly 100–110 chars across the full 12.1in content width. Bold is ~8% wider than regular — estimate with the checker, not by eye.
    47	- Set `font.name` on every run; mixed fonts within a slide look broken. "Segoe UI" is safe cross-platform for generated decks; "Arial" is the conservative fallback.
    48	- `word_wrap = True` and zero text-frame margins (inset) are non-negotiable for precise sizing; the default insets are 0.1in all around and silently steal width.
    49	
    50	(see "Transitions (working recipe, verified)" section below for the concrete zip patch)
    51	
    52	## Charts
    53	
    54	- `from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData` + `slide.shapes.add_chart(chart_type, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data)`.
    55	- 16:9: a column/bar chart needs at least 4.5in × 3.5in; a line chart 5in wide. Put a caption below it (13pt, muted), not inside it.
    56	- Style the chart with `chart.font` / per-series `format.fill` to match the palette; default Office charts are blue-and-dirty-gray and clash with custom palettes.
    57	- For a "stat row" (numbers + label), plain rounded-rectangle cards beat a real chart — a chart implies trend, a stat row implies magnitudes.
    58	
    59	## Errors this deck hit, and the fix
    60	
    61	1. **Text overflow that looks fine at 100%**: 54pt two-line title in a 1.6in box rendered OK but left no headroom; the checker flagged it. Fix: give title boxes the height of *max possible lines × size × 1.3*, not the current text. Budget per line: `size_pt × 1.3 / 72` inches.
    62	2. **White checkmark on a light rounded-rect**: I drew the white ✓ in a box that had a light fill; contrast 1.05. Fix: the ✓ sits on the *accent* chip — make the chip the accent fill (0.4×0.4in rounded) with white text; the checker only trusts the panel it finds *under* the text, so the chip must actually be drawn before the text and fully contain it.
    63	3. **Checker false negative — text on slide bg**: `bg_of()` returned the slide background instead of the card the text sat on, flagging every card text as low-contrast. Fix: pick the **smallest** filled shape that contains the text box; fall back to slide bg. (This is a checker bug, not a deck bug — but the fix matters because an always-red checker stops being trusted.)
    64	4. **Save path**: `prs.save("deck1.pptx")` fails when run from the wrong cwd; save via `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), name)`.
    65	
    66	## Checklist before calling a deck done
    67	
    68	- [ ] `check_deck.py` prints "clean" (no overflow flags, no overlaps, no <12pt, no contrast <3.0).
    69	- [ ] `soffice` conversion produces a PDF with the same page count as the slide count.
    70	- [ ] Every content slide has a header zone (kicker + title + rule) and nothing starts above 1.8in.
    71	- [ ] Each slide states one idea; body text ≤ ~3 short lines per card.
    72	- [ ] No shape exceeds slide bounds; text never within 0.15in of the slide edge.

def rect(s, x, y, w, h, color, radius=False):
    shape_type = MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE if radius else MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE
    sh = s.shapes.add_shape(shape_type, x, y, w, h)
    sh.fill.solid()
    sh.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    sh.line.fill.background()
    sh.shadow.inherit = False
    return sh


def text(s, x, y, w, h, runs, size=16, color=INK, bold=False,
         align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP, line_spacing=1.0,
         space_after=6):
    tb = s.shapes.add_textbox(x, y, w, h)
    tf = tb.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.vertical_anchor = anchor
    tf.margin_left = tf.margin_right = tf.margin_top = tf.margin_bottom = 0
    first = True
    for para in runs:
        p = tf.paragraphs[0] if first else tf.add_paragraph()
        first = False
        p.alignment = align
        p.line_spacing = line_spacing
        p.space_after = Pt(space_after)
        items = [(para, color, bold)] if isinstance(para, str) else para
        for t, c, b in items:
            r = p.add_run()
            r.text = t
            r.font.name = FONT
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
            r.font.bold = b
            r.font.color.rgb = c
    return tb

## Tổng kết kiến trúc manga-translator

### 5 lớp chính

| Lớp | Mô tả | Thư mục / file chính |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Presentation** | React + Vite frontend (serve static, Tailwind) | `app/static/` — app.html, app.js, assets |
| **2. API / Router** | 12 FastAPI routers, ~100+ endpoints | `app/routers/` — chapters, editor, export, ocr, translation, ai_mode, agent, visual_qc, account, automation, image, render |
| **3. Domain Logic** | Pipeline xử lý + các module chức năng | `app/pipeline.py`, `app/detector/`, `app/inpaint/`, `app/ocr/`, `app/render/`, `app/translation/`, `app/downloader/` |
| **4. Infrastructure** | Config, security, data, models, gateway | `app/config.py`, `app/security.py`, `data/`, `models/`, `gateway/` |
| **5. Agent / AI** | LLM agent + AI mode pipeline + Visual QC | `app/agent/`, `app/ai_mode/`, `app/visual_qc/` |

### Điểm đáng chú ý
- **ChapterPipeline** (`app/pipeline.py`) là xương sống: download → Lama inpaint → detect → OCR → translate → render → export, mỗi bước có checkpoint riêng.
- **`gateway/`** là FastAPI app **riêng** (không nằm trong app chính) làm proxy LLM + billing + quota, tách bạch về mặt tiến trình.
- **`app/manifest_utils.py`** giữ mọi cập nhật file qua file lock + atomic write — manifest.json là nguồn truth metadata.
- **`app/security.py`** chặn SSRF (private IP, localhost), giới hạn upload, validate path — chạy xuyên suốt mọi router.
- **AI Mode** (`app/ai_mode/`) chạy 8 bước tự động (scan → clean → review → translate → polish → render → finish), dùng cùng endpoint với editor nên locking/revision đồng nhất.

### Slide trong deck (11 trang)
1. **Title** — bìa
2. **Tổng quan** — cây thư mục cao cấp
3. **ChapterPipeline** — 7 bước luồng xử lý
4. **Modules** — detector, inpaint, ocr, render, translation, ai_mode, visual_qc, agent
5. **Routers** — 12 router (3 hàng × 4 card)
6. **Gateway** — billing, store, mailer, routes
7. **AI Mode** — 8 checkpoint
8. **Manga Agent** — session, tools, skills, MCP, plugins
9. **Dữ liệu** — data/raw → processed → output → models (luồng)
10. **Bảo mật** — 6 nhóm giới hạn
11. **Tổng kết** — 5 lớp kiến trúc
